description.description: What the agent is for. Hosts that list agents show it.

instructions.description: Markdown files, relative to this file, joined in order to form the system prompt.

skills.description: Paths to Agent Skills folders, relative to this file. Each folder holds a SKILL.md.

permissions.description: Narrows how the agent may use its tools.

limits.description: Bounds each run of the agent.

output.description: What the agent's final answer must look like. Part of the agent's identity: targets can't change it.

vaults.description: Vaults whose credentials the agent may use, by reference to Vault resources. Once an agent lists any, every secret its MCP servers need must come from one of them, and the run gets nothing else.

workspace.description: The folder the agent works on, and whether it may change it. Each target says which folder, in spec.inputs.workspace.

repositories.description: Git repositories the agent works on. Each target binds every name to a URL in spec.inputs.repositories, and the repository is cloned into repositories/<name> in the workspace before a run.

providers.description: Fields passed unchanged to one provider, keyed by provider name. Using them makes the agent less portable, and validate reports it.

AgentSpec.description: Describes an agent independently of the host it runs on.

maxTurns.description: Most model calls in one run.

timeout.description: Longest a run may take, as a duration such as 30m or 1h30m.

LimitsSpec.description: Bounds each run of an agent.

allowTools.description: The server's tools this agent may call. When omitted, every tool the server offers is allowed.

MCPToolRef.description: References an McpServer and narrows which of its tools the agent may call.

preferred.description: Preferred model, as provider:model, for example anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5.

fallback.description: Fallback models, tried in order on hosts that support fallback.

effort.description: How much reasoning the model should spend. Providers map it to the closest setting their host has.

ModelSpec.description: Selects a model as provider:model strings.

name.description: Unique name per kind. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters.

labels.description: Labels for selecting resources, for example from a Target's agents.selector.

annotations.description: Notes about how the resource is operated rather than what it is, such as an agent's owner, trigger or target autonomy. Keys are like label keys; values are any text. They're never part of a digest or sent to a host, so changing one changes nothing deployed. solaria status -o json shows an agent's.

oneOf.description: Path to a JSON or YAML file holding the schema.

schema.description: The JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) the agent's final answer must match: either a path to a JSON or YAML file, relative to this file, or the schema itself, written in YAML. Its root must be an object schema, since the answer is one JSON object. Plan fails on a host that can't enforce it.

OutputSpec.description: Says what the agent's final answer must look like.

ask.description: Tools that need a person's approval before each call: a builtin name, or server/tool for an MCP tool. On hosts without approvals in unattended runs, these tools are denied, and plan says so.

PermissionsSpec.description: Narrows how the agent may use its tools.

name.description: Name the target binds the repository under, and its folder in the workspace: repositories/<name>.

access.description: read-only or read-write: whether the agent may change its clone. A placement that can't keep a clone read-only fails plan rather than ignore it.

RepositoryNeed.description: A repository an agent works on, and what it may do to its copy.

builtin.description: Builtin tools, by Solaria's host-neutral names. Providers map them to their host's own tools.

mcp.description: MCP servers the agent uses, by reference to McpServer resources.

ToolsSpec.description: Lists the tools an agent may use. Tools not listed are not available.

access.description: read-write (the default) or read-only. A placement that can't keep the workspace read-only fails plan rather than ignore it.

WorkspaceSpec.description: What an agent may do to its workspace.

title: Solaria Agent
description: Declares what an agent is: its instructions, model, tools, skills and limits. Where it runs is decided by a Target.
